subject: Logic
title: Archimedes and the Sand
description: A 60-second lesson on Archimedes and the Sand.

hook.text: How many grains of sand would fill the entire universe? Most Greeks said infinity. Archimedes said: let me count.

buildup.text: In The Sand Reckoner, Archimedes invented a notation for enormous numbers to show the universe is finite and countable.

discovery.text: He estimated the universe's diameter, calculated its volume, and counted sand grains. Answer: about 10 to the 63rd.

twist.text: The real breakthrough wasn't the number—it was proving that infinity isn't needed to describe the physical world.

climax.text: He showed large doesn't mean infinite—a distinction that still confuses people today.

punchline.text: Even the universe has a number.

quiz.question: What did Archimedes prove in The Sand Reckoner?
options: Very large quantities are still finite and countable
Sand grains are too small to count
